data.title: PAT ZONE ASSESSMENT 🚧
data.statement:
Before entering, PAT assesses a zone. It measures the <<rectangular>> safe perimeter survivors must hold, and the <<spherical>> volume a Grinder drone can scan.

Given the safe perimeter's length [[L]] and width [[W]] in <<meters>>, the drone's detection radius [[R]] in <<meters>>, Paul's ground position ([[Px]], [[Py]]) and the drone's flying position ([[Dx]], [[Dy]], [[Dz]]), output:

the safe perimeter: 2 × ([[W]] + [[H]])
the drone detection volume: (4/3) × {{π}} × [[R]]³
whether the zone is safe: {{true}} if PAT is outside the drone's detection sphere, else {{false}}

PAT stands on the ground, so it's Pz doesn't must be computed. The drone detects PAT when the 3D <<distance>> between them is ≤ [[R]]. Every number and formula result is ceil rounded and expressed in <<meters>>.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Before entering, PAT assesses a zone. It measures the rectangular safe perimeter survivors must hold, and the spherical volume a Grinder drone can scan.

Given the safe perimeter's length L and width W in meters, the drone's detection radius R in meters, Paul's ground position (Px, Py) and the drone's flying position (Dx, Dy, Dz), output:

the safe perimeter: 2 × (W + H)
the drone detection volume: (4/3) × π × R³
whether the zone is safe: true if PAT is outside the drone's detection sphere, else false

PAT stands on the ground, so it's Pz doesn't must be computed. The drone detects PAT when the 3D distance between them is ≤ R. Every number and formula result is ceil rounded and expressed in meters.
Input
Line 1: Three space-separated integers L, W and R.
Line 2: Two space-separated integers Px and Py.
Line 3: Three space-separated integers Dx, Dy and Dz.
Output
Line 1: An integer, the safe perimeter in meter, ceil rounded.
Line 2: An integer, the drone detection volume in meter, ceil rounded.
Line 3: A boolean, whether the zone is safe.
Constraints
1 ≤ L, W ≤ 999
1 ≤ R ≤ 99
0 ≤ Px, Py, Dx, Dy, Dz ≤ 999
Example
Input
3 4 5
0 0
10 10 10
Output
14
524
true
